data.description:
Found by the evidence pass on ticket sole-curbable-stinkpot (9a71-ba9b-89d0-4cb8). The original sweep believed this string was aborting passes; it is NOT. It is silently swallowed noise, which is its own defect.

Observed in 6 failed runs (31535962079, 31455622724, 31420498173, 31244501098, 31129551929, 31129431096), 15-21 occurrences per run:

    ACLI stderr: X Error: command cancelled

Characteristics:
- First appears immediately after 'RECON: typed_inbound_dispatched count=16' (or 19), i.e. at the START of the outbound update / link-apply batch loop, 2-6 minutes into the job.
- Each occurrence is bracketed by a SUCCESSFUL 'RECON: batch_outcome action=update key=REB-... error=None links_applied=N'. The enclosing operation is recorded as SUCCEEDING.
- No exit code, no HTTP status, no traceback, no reconciler-level ERROR is attached.
- In the 08-06/08-08 runs the lines are ~6.3s apart, 1-2 per ticket, which looks like a per-call timeout/retry inside the link-apply path rather than a one-off.
- 'unauthorized' count is 0 in all six runs: this is NOT the credential failure surfacing.

Why it matters: some ACLI call is being aborted and the reconciler records the containing operation as applied. That is the same silent-divergence class as bug 44de (ACLI exit 0 on a failed mutation) and is exactly what REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP exists to catch, yet it is not caught here.

A strong lead worth checking FIRST: acli_graph.py passes '--yes' to 'workitem edit --from-json' with an explicit comment that '--from-json writes require --yes to skip the interactive confirmation', but 'workitem link create' and 'workitem link delete' pass NO '--yes'. Subprocesses run with stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, so a confirmation prompt would get EOF, which a Go CLI reports as 'command cancelled'. Note story 25ae found the installed ACLI rejects '--json' on those same link subcommands, so verify '--yes' is accepted before adding it.

Scope: identify which call is cancelled, stop swallowing it, and make the enclosing batch_outcome reflect the real result.
data.title: ACLI 'command cancelled' is emitted and swallowed during the outbound link-apply loop
